module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 552

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/552](https://www.erdosproblems.com/552)
- [BEFRS89] Burr, S. and Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., Some
  complete bipartite graph-tree Ramsey numbers. Graph theory in memory of G. A. Dirac (Sandbjerg,
  1985) (1989), 79-89.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos552

/--
Determine the Ramsey number
$$R(C_4, S_n),$$
where $S_n=K_{1,n}$ is the star on $n+1$ vertices.

A problem of Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp [BEFRS89].

This problem is #19 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_552.parts.i :
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4)
        (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 1) (Fin n)) =
        answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
In particular, is it true that, for any $c > 0$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$R(C_4, S_n) \leq n + \sqrt{n} - c?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_552.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c →
      Set.Infinite {n : ℕ |
        (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4)
          (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 1) (Fin n)) : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) + Real.sqrt n - c} := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos552

reformulations.difference: The cited primary paper, BEFRS89 §4, states the infinite-subsequence question using f(n) < n + √n − c′ for arbitrary constants. Lean uses ≤ and explicitly restricts the universally quantified constant to c > 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any real c, apply the Lean condition with d = max(c, 0) + 1. Then d > 0 and d > c, so every n satisfying f(n) ≤ n + √n − d also satisfies f(n) < n + √n − c; infinitude is preserved under inclusion. Conversely, the strict condition for every constant immediately implies the weak condition for every positive constant. This equivalence was proved for an arbitrary real-valued sequence in /workspace/review/boundary.lean, without sorry.

sources_consulted: Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, Some complete bipartite graph-tree Ramsey numbers (1989), §§1–2 and 4, especially pp. 80 and 88–89: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1989-32.pdf
review.notes: Both declarations faithfully express the questions in the cited primary paper. Checked graphRamsey, ordinary (not induced) containment, graph complements, the cycle and star constructors, answer-slot scope, and real arithmetic. Finite Ramsey theory ensures the defining sInf set is nonempty. Independent Lean proofs establish R(C₄,K₁,₀)=1 and R(C₄,K₁,₁)=4; further tests confirm the star has n+1 vertices and that n=0 cannot satisfy part ii's inequality when c>0. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/552 and OEIS was blocked by Cloudflare despite a descriptive User-Agent. Mathematical verification therefore used BEFRS89; the accessible community database corroborates the recorded open status, but the live website's latest remarks could not be checked.
